content.comment_body: Hello, I have a motor and want to conduct some tests. The motor has a two-wire NTC output—can I send 24V through it and connect it to [article_no] ([product_name]), or do I need the RTD [product_name] to accomplish this? Best regards [user_name]
Neither option will work. You require a proper evaluation device for this purpose! Regards, [user_name] (translation via Google)
The RTD [product_name] is designed only for PT100/PT1000 sensors; it does not support NTC sensors. Do you have details regarding the specific type of NTC?
Hi, Thank you for your response. The NTC specifications are: TDK NTCG164KF104F Temperature range: -40°C to 125°C, Resistance: 100 kΩ, B25/100 = 4508 K Best regards [user_name]
Based on calculations using the datasheet, it appears that connecting the NTC directly to 24VDC will result in excessive current through the sensor, making this approach unsuitable.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to connect a two-wire NTC sensor from a motor to a [company_name] hardware module and exploring whether the RTD [product_name] can be used. The feedback highlights that neither direct connection with 24VDC nor use of the RTD module is compatible with the sensor, revealing a lack of suitable accessories for matching sensor types and causing some uncertainty.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates being able to easily connect or adapt a standard two-wire NTC sensor to [product_name], ideally expecting built-in compatibility or a matching [product_name] for expansion.
